title: Pierogi Ruskie
subtitle: Polish potato and cheese dumplings
excerpt: Soft dumplings filled with mashed potato and onion, boiled then pan-fried in butter until golden at the edges. Pierogi ruskie are the most common variety of Poland's most iconic dish. They take time but the process is straightforward.
sourceNotes: Pierogi are Poland's most iconic dish. Ruskie -- meaning 'Ruthenian' -- are filled with potato and white cheese. They are boiled then pan-fried in butter for crisp edges.

content.text: Pierogi ruskie take patience but no advanced skill. The dough is simple, the filling is potato and onion, and the final pan-fry in butter gives them their characteristic golden edges. Serve with soured cream and more fried onion on top.

items.prepNote: 3 tbsp for filling, remainder to serve

content.text: Make the dough: mix flour, egg, milk, and a pinch of salt. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover with a cloth and rest for 20 minutes.
Fry 1 diced onion in butter until golden and soft. This goes into the filling.
Mix the fried onion with mashed potato, 3 tbsp soured cream, salt, and pepper. Taste and season well.
Roll dough thin on a floured surface. Cut circles about 8cm wide.
Place 1 tbsp filling in the centre of each circle. Fold over and pinch the edges very firmly together.
Boil in batches in a large pot of salted water for 4-5 minutes until they float and look glossy. Drain.
Pan-fry in butter over medium-high heat until golden on each side. Fry the remaining diced onion separately. Serve topped with fried onion and soured cream.

items.cause: Filling too wet or edges not sealed properly
items.fix: Squeeze out any excess moisture from the filling and press edges firmly, dampening with a little water to help them stick.

content.text: Poland and Ukrainian borderlands. Street food, restaurant food, and home food. The ruskie variety is the most common across Poland -- simple, filling, and deeply satisfying.
